User: I'm going through a legal process and need to organize my thoughts. The case involves nondisclosure agreement dispute. My lawyer is Lisa Park with Park Legal Group; we have proceedings at the federal district court. We're past the filing stage and waiting for the court calendar.. Opposing party: my former landlord. This is in King County, Washington. The contract was signed last year and they've since stopped performing. Can you help me figure out what to ask my attorney about what documents I should bring and what to say in the hearing? I want to be ready for the legal next steps.
Assistant: I can help — below is a focused, practical checklist you can use to prepare for your meeting with Lisa Park and for any upcoming hearing. If you want, I can draft an email to Lisa with this list (or send it) — tell me whether you want it sent now and to which address.

1) Essential case details to have ready
- Case name and federal docket/case number
- Court name (U.S. District Court — Western District of Washington, King County) and judge if assigned
- Your counsel’s contact info (Lisa Park, Park Legal Group)
- Current procedural posture (you said: past filing, waiting for court calendar) and any pending motions or deadlines

2) Documents to bring (organize into a binder and also have digital copies)
- The signed nondisclosure agreement (NDA) — complete original and any amendments
- Chronological timeline (one‑page summary + detailed timeline) of events from signing to present
- All communications relating to the NDA and performance (emails, texts, letters) — include dates, senders/recipients
- Evidence of the opposing party’s nonperformance (what they failed to do, dates, and any direct consequences)
- Any notices you gave (demand letters, cure notices, reminder emails) and their delivery proof (read receipts, certified mail receipts)
- Lease or landlord documents (if relevant to dispute context) showing relationship and any relevant clauses tying landlord duties to the NDA
- Financial records showing damages or losses (invoices, bank statements, receipts) if you’re claiming monetary harm
- Prior court filings: complaint, summons, proof of service, any answers/counterclaims, motions already filed, declarations you already filed
- Docket printout (from PACER or the court website) showing current status and pending items
- Witness contact list and brief summaries of what each witness can attest to
- Any prior settlement offers/communications and insurance correspondence (if applicable)
- Identification (government ID) and counsel engagement letter/fee agreement

3) Documents the court will likely want (ask Lisa to confirm)
- Proposed exhibit list with exhibit labels (Ex. 1, Ex. 2, etc.)
- Copies of all exhibits for the court, the judge, opposing counsel, and your counsel (typically 3–4 sets)
- Proposed orders (if you’re asking the court for relief like injunctive relief or scheduling)
- Proposed scheduling order or statement of requested deadlines (if a scheduling/status conference is coming)

4) Questions to ask Lisa Park (bring this list into your meeting)
Logistics / process
- What is the likely calendar event next (scheduling conference, status hearing, motion hearing)? How long are those hearings typically?
- Is the hearing in-person or telephonic/video? What should I expect on the day (where to be, when to arrive)?
- How long will I have to speak? Will I be required to testify at this stage?
- What filings or disclosures must be completed before the next court date?

Evidence & documents
- Which documents are most critical to bring to the hearing? Which can be submitted later as declarations or exhibits?
- Which documents should be filed as exhibits now vs. kept for discovery/trial?
- Are there authentication steps we need for emails/texts (metadata, affidavits)?

Legal strategy & likely outcomes
- What is our legal theory and what relief will we ask the court to grant at the next hearing (e.g., preliminary injunction, damages, expedited discovery)?
- What defenses should I expect the landlord to raise?
- What is the standard of proof for the relief we want at this stage?
- What weaknesses do you see in our case and how should I address them?

Witnesses & testimony
- Do we need witnesses at the hearing? If so, who? Will written declarations be sufficient?
- Should I prepare a short, factual statement? What points must I emphasize?

Practical prep & settlement
- Do you recommend any pre‑hearing settlement outreach? Acceptable settlement range?
- Estimated timeline for discovery, motions, and trial
- Cost exposure and fee strategies (fee shifting, seeking attorneys’ fees)

Court rules & formatting
- Any local rules or judge preferences we must follow (page limits, exhibit format, delivery instructions)?
- How do we submit exhibits to the court (electronic filing format via CM/ECF, or paper copies) and deadlines?

5) What to say at the hearing — short scripts / pointers
- Opening/summary (concise, 30–90 seconds): “Your Honor, I’m [Your Name], plaintiff. The NDA was signed on [date]. The defendant stopped performing on [date], despite our written demands on [dates]. We ask the court for [specific relief — e.g., scheduling, expedited discovery, preliminary relief] so we can prevent further harm and move this case forward. Our key exhibit is Ex. 1 (the NDA) and Ex. 2 (notice of breach).”
- When the judge asks for facts: Be concise and factual. Use the timeline: “On [date], I sent an email (Ex. 3). The landlord failed to [action], which led to [specific harm].”
- If asked about remedy: State what you want and why it’s appropriate: “We request [injunction/specific deadline] because [consequence].”
- If you don’t know an answer: Say “I don’t know; I’ll defer to counsel,” or “I don’t recall — I can provide that information to the court through counsel with the document.”
- Avoid arguing with the judge or opposing counsel, and avoid volunteering extra details beyond the question asked.
- Always refer to exhibits by their exhibit number when citing evidence.

6) How to organize your materials
- One-page executive timeline + index
- Exhibit binder with tabs and an exhibit index (electronic folder mirroring binder)
- Copies: one for the judge (if paper filing required), one for clerk, one for opposing counsel, one for you/counsel
- Highlighted passages in NDA and emails with sticky flags for quick reference
- Prepare a short “talking points” sheet (3–5 bullets) for the hearing

7) Practical courtroom tips
- Dress conservatively and arrive early (30–60 minutes)
- Turn off phone; bring chargers/backup electronic copies on a thumb drive
- Speak clearly and address the judge as “Your Honor”
- Let your attorney lead; answer only what’s asked
- If remote, test connection and camera/mic beforehand

8) Next‑steps checklist to do now
- Create the timeline (I can help draft it from your notes)
- Collect and scan the NDA and all communications — name files clearly by date
- Make an exhibit index and label exhibits
- Send the document package to Lisa at least X days before the hearing — ask her for preferred format
- Schedule a prep call with Lisa to run through likely questions / practice your short statement

Would you like me to:
- Draft an email to Lisa Park containing this checklist and asking her which specific documents she wants and how she prefers them submitted? (If yes, tell me whether to save as a draft or send it and which email address to use.)
- Help create the one‑page timeline or an exhibit index from the documents you have (you can upload or paste key dates/entries)?

Tell me how you’d like to proceed and I’ll draft the email or help build the timeline/exhibit list.
